chapter_note: A compact five-fold, impersonal classification of the operations of fire. Aside from the brief dialogue/frame attribution in ¶1, the chapter is a self-contained systematic teaching sequence with no NT citation, no institutional application, and no cosmos→contemporary-world pointing.

paragraphs.core_text: This fire, which burns and is apparent today in the world, it does five works.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the hagiographic/dialogue frame attribution: “Once more he speaks:” (later compilation frame).
paragraphs.temporal_note: The opening speech-attribution is a classic Kephalaia frame marker; the remaining sentence initiates a numbered five-fold teaching list in an impersonal, classificatory voice.

paragraphs.core_text: The first work that it does is this: It incinerates and burns wood, and everything that shall be placed upon it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered, impersonal expository style continuing the five-work structure; no citation or exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: The second: It separates four aspects of the wood, which are these: fire and light, ash and smoke.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic analytic division (four aspects) embedded inside the larger five-fold; characteristic of classificatory substrate teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: The third: It gives a taste and an aroma to whatever will be cooked on it. It also gives heat and cheer to whoever will be close to it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the numbered list with sensory/affective effects (taste/aroma/heat/cheer) stated descriptively, not applied to church life or ethics.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth work that [it] does: All craftsmen shall work the utensils that they will fabricate in it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Still within the same five-work classification; practical effect described without present-tense polemic or institutional address.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth: It shall display light, and the people see by [it].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Concludes the five-fold sequence; closes naturally as a complete classificatory set, consistent with a core teaching unit.
